record.what_it_does: Open-source CLI that checks a username across 400+ social networks to find accounts.
record.auth_notes: There is no hosted API and no authentication. Sherlock is a local MIT-licensed Python CLI, installed with pipx, Docker or dnf. Neither the GitHub README nor sherlockproject.xyz mentions an API, hosted service, accounts or pricing. Third-party hosted wrappers such as Apify actors use their own tokens.
record.access_notes: The vendor offers no hosted service and issues no credentials. You run the tool yourself for free (pipx install sherlock-project, docker run sherlock/sherlock, or dnf install). Serving many users means hosting it on your own infrastructure.
record.api_breadth_notes: Only a CLI exists. It looks up usernames across 400+ sites and has export, site-filter, proxy and timeout options. There is no REST or other network API.
record.mcp_notes: There is no official MCP server from sherlock-project. The relevant community wrapper is Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp, a FastMCP stdio server with one search_username tool that shells out to the Sherlock CLI. Several servers share the name but are unrelated: H4RR1SON/covertlabs "Sherlock MCP" is for Covertlabs infostealer intelligence, and Fewsats/sherlock-mcp on PyPI is for buying domains.
record.blocker_notes: Sherlock is a local CLI with no hosted API or auth. A toolkit would have to run the CLI (or Docker image) on infrastructure Composio hosts. The other option is a third-party Apify actor, which is a separate product with its own billing.
